title: BioMedStatX – Statistical workflows for reliable biomedical data analysis
author: Krumm, Böttcher, et al.

steps.title: Prepare data file
steps.instruction: Arrange the experimental measurements in a long‑format spreadsheet (Excel *.xlsx or CSV) with two columns: one named “Group” containing the categorical condition (e.g., treatment groups) and one named “Values” containing the numeric measurement for each data point.

steps.title: Load data into BioMedStatX
steps.instruction: Open BioMedStatX, click the “Browse…” button, locate the prepared file, select the appropriate worksheet (if Excel), and specify the “Group” column and the “Values” column; the program will automatically read and list all groups.

steps.title: Select groups and optional plot settings
steps.instruction: Choose which groups to analyse (you may create multiple analyses from the same data). If desired, customise plot appearance (type, colours, hatches, axis labels, titles, error bars, etc.) before running the analysis; plots are optional and can be omitted.

steps.title: Start the analysis
steps.instruction: Press either the “Create and analyze all plots” button to generate plots and run statistics, or the “Create selected plot” button to run statistics without generating all plots.

steps.title: Automatic assumption checks
steps.instruction: The software first determines the number of groups, then performs a Shapiro‑Wilk test for normality and a Levene (Brown‑Forsythe) test for homoscedasticity on the raw data.

steps.title: Choose data transformation if needed
steps.instruction: If the assumption checks indicate non‑normality or heteroscedasticity, select one of the three transformation options offered: Log10, Box‑Cox (λ estimated by maximum‑likelihood method), or Arcsine‑Square‑Root.

steps.title: Re‑check assumptions and run appropriate test
steps.instruction: After transformation, the program repeats the Shapiro‑Wilk and Levene tests on the transformed data. Based on the results it automatically selects a parametric test (e.g., One‑Way ANOVA, Repeated‑Measures ANOVA, t‑test, paired t‑test) or the corresponding non‑parametric test (e.g., Kruskal‑Wallis, Mann‑Whitney‑U, Wilcoxon‑Signed‑Rank).

steps.title: Select post‑hoc test after significant ANOVA
steps.instruction: If the chosen ANOVA yields a significant result, pick a post‑hoc comparison method from the menu: Tukey‑HSD, Dunnett, or Šídák; you may also select specific pairs of means for comparison.

steps.title: Export results
steps.instruction: The software automatically writes all statistical outputs—including descriptive statistics, assumption test p‑values, selected test results, effect sizes, outlier flags, and the decision tree—to an Excel workbook with multiple sheets (Summary, Assumptions, Statistical Results, Descriptive Statistics, Decision Tree, Raw Data, Pairwise Comparisons, Analysis Log). Plots can be saved as PNG or SVG files.
